doorbell.name: Doorbell
doorbell.note:
Press the button and the machine answers

No model here at all. Press Run, then press the Button: the wire carries the press to the Sound and the Lamp — the machine answers because YOU wired it to. Change the Lamp colour or the Sound voice on their plates and press again.

Build the doorbell
1. Drag a Button, a Sound and a Lamp from the shelf onto the floor.
2. Drag a wire from the Button's pressed socket to the Sound's play socket.
3. Drag another wire from pressed to the Lamp's on socket.
4. Press Run, then press the Button.
Guess first, then try: pick a different voice on the Sound's plate and press again — what changes?

reactor.name: Reactor
reactor.note:
A counter for energy, a clock that drains it, a sealed monitor part that judges it — and a second copy of that part wired back in as an automatic regulator

No model here — this is a machine about wiring, counting and one part used twice. Press Run: the Energy counter is the reactor, the Timer drains it one point every 3 seconds, and Charge, Vent and Reset are your hands. The Energy reading rides ONE wire into the sealed Reactor monitor, which judges it — below 3 lights LOW, above 7 lights OVERHEATING, 3 to 7 lights SAFE — and averages the last five readings. Tap its little window to see the five Filters and the Window inside. The SAME part stands beside it a second time as the Automatic regulator, with its low and hot outputs wired back into the counter: low charges, hot vents. Sit back and watch it hold the energy in range with nobody pressing anything — that closed loop is control. Try to make the Announcer say "Meltdown!" (the counter fires at 10): you cannot while the regulator is wired. Unplug the regulator's hot wire and try again.

wastesorter.name: Waste sorter
wastesorter.note:
Taught from real TrashNet photos, tested on the live camera — one belt, one Model, and a points switch the wires throw

The Files block holds 18 real photos of paper, metal and plastic and hands them to the Splitter, which divides them into Training, Validation (Dev) and Test piles. Press Run, then "Teach it": the training photos ride the belt and the Material reader FILES each one instead of guessing — watch its shelves fill. Every photo the Splitter deals also throws the Route switch to way 2, so those crates end at the Evaluator, not in a bin. Press "Test on new": the held-out photos ride the same belt, the reader guesses, and the Evaluator scores them — that number is how well it learned. Open the Evaluator’s log for Learn, check, improve: compare Training and Dev, change only neighbours k, inspect the measured curve, then choose a model and run final Test. The small piles are a lesson, not proof of reliable recycling. Now the live part: hold a real can, paper or plastic up to the Camera and press "Show it something". The Camera's picture throws the Route switch back to way 1, so this crate rides on to the sorter gate and lands in the bin the reader chose — Paper, Metal, Plastic, or Not sure when the reader is not confident. The Voice says each reading out loud. Two wires decide which route a crate takes; read them.

guardian.name: Guardian
guardian.note:
A camera eye taught what "normal" looks like barks at anything new — three barks call the alarm, ten quiet seconds say all clear, once

The Guardian knows nothing yet. Open Teach on it and snap the room as it usually looks onto a shelf named normal — a few photos. Press Run: the Camera snaps every 2 seconds, and the Guardian reads each picture as the crate rides past. Anything it was not taught fires unsure: the Lamp, the Sound and the Barks counter all hang off that one wire. At the third bark the counter fires and reads the "Intruder!" Memory into the Voice and the Status sign. Then stand still: after 10 quiet seconds the Timer fires — but a quiet timer fires again every 10 seconds, so a Counter set to 1 stands between it and the "All clear" Memory and lets it speak only once; any new bark resets that counter. Trace the once-latch: it is three blocks, and every guard dog needs one.

repcounter.name: Rep counter
repcounter.note:
Raise and lower your arms in front of the camera — a Memory turns pose readings into reps, and every rep is a higher note

Open Teach on the Pose reader: snap yourself with arms DOWN onto a shelf named arms down, then arms UP onto a shelf named arms up — a few of each. Press Run and do slow jumping jacks. The reader says the pose on every picture, so while your arms stay up it keeps saying "arms up" — that would count one rep as five. So the reading goes into a Memory, and only the Memory's CHANGED port reaches the Filter and the Reps counter: a rep is a change to arms up, nothing else. The count rides a dial wire into the Note's pitch through a Calculate that adds 60, so each rep plays higher than the last. At ten the Lamp lights and the Voice cheers. Press "Start again" to zero it.

grouper.name: k-Means sorter
grouper.note:
Nobody names the bins — the machine invents its piles

This sorter has ONE shelf. Open Teach on the Front door and snap all sorts of things onto a shelf named stuff — a dozen or more. Run, show them again: k-Means sends each to the pile it invented. Open the bins and decide what it found.

mira.name: Mira, the camera creature
mira.note:
Teach it two objects — it answers each with a trick it picks by luck, and rewarding a trick makes it pick that one more

Press Run, then "Try trick": the Trick preference is a Chance block set to pick one of three named faces, and its pick rides into the sealed Mira tricks part, which plays that trick's sound and remembers it; the Last-trick sign and the Voice name it. Press "Reward shown trick": the face just picked gets heavier on the Chance card — that is reinforcement learning, in one block. Now Stop, open Teach on "Teach two objects" and snap several photos of two different things onto two shelves. Run, hold one up and press "Show object": the Model recognises it, the Frame shows the nearest photo it kept, and the reading rides into the same Chance — every recognised object earns a trick. Something it was not taught goes down the unsure wire into the New-object path part, which says "Teach me?" instead. Leave it alone for 18 seconds and the Quiet lookout part asks to play, once. Tap any part's little window to see how it is built.

pieces.faceNames: Star turn | Orbit bounce | Comet chirp
pieces.name: Trick preference

nearest.name: Nearest example
nearest.note:
Teach it a few pictures, then show it something new — it retrieves the closest saved picture; it does not generate a new one

Open Teach on the Picture reader and snap a few pictures onto a few named shelves — a cup, a ball, whatever is nearby. Press Run, then press "Show it something" and hold one of those things up to the Camera: the Sign names it, and the Frame shows the EXACT photo it matched to — the closest one it kept, not a new one.

voiceremote.name: Voice remote
voiceremote.note:
Teach it four colour words, then say one — the matching Lamp lights and the Voice confirms; the decision is your own word model's

Open Teach on the Colour word reader and add four words by hand — type red, then type red again as its own shelf, press Add; the same for green, blue and yellow. Press Run, press Listen and say one of them: the Microphone hears it and drops it on the belt as a crate, the reader answers with the closest word it knows, and that reading fans out along four wires — four Filters, each guarding one Lamp. Only the matching Lamp lights, and the Voice repeats the word. Say something it was never taught: nothing lights, and the sign says "not sure". Then teach it a fifth word and add a fifth lamp yourself. The first time anyone presses Listen, the Workshop asks whether the Microphone may use the browser's speech service — say Allow for the lesson; Not now leaves every Microphone honestly blocked.

selftrain.name: Self-training sorter
selftrain.note:
It files every crate it deals — then feed it its own guesses

Run: the stamper files each crate as it enters, and the eye starts sorting once a few are on the shelf. The experiment: Cable the eye’s reading to the feeder’s drop — now it studies its own guesses. Watch what one mistake becomes.

irislab.name: Iris lab
irislab.note:
Real flower measurements — study some, test the rest, and a Board that watches k so the overfitting picture draws itself

Real data: 30 Iris flowers measured by botanists — four lengths each, three species. The Files block hands them to the Splitter, which divides them into Training, Validation and Test piles. Press Run, then "Teach it": the training rows ride past the Iris reader, which FILES each one — k-Nearest Neighbours stores examples, it does not fit a line. "Test what it studied" deals those same rows again and the reader GUESSES; the Evaluator scores them under Training. "Test on new" deals the Validation rows, scored in their own column — the gap is the lesson. The Board watches k: after each test a point lands. Set k to 1, teach, test both — then 5, then 9. Which k remembers the studied rows perfectly, and which does best on new ones? The Test pile has a release nobody wired, on purpose: that is the sealed exam.

icecream.name: Ice-cream stand
icecream.note:
How MANY, not which one — teach it, test what it studied, test on new; the rule it fits is one you can read

The table of ice-cream days is not in the Feeder — the Files block holds it and hands its rows to the Splitter beside it, which divides them into Training, Validation and Test piles by the bar on its own face and holds every pile back until one of its acts fires. Press Run, then work the three Buttons in order. "Teach it" deals the Training pile past the Cups reader, which FILES every crate instead of guessing — its line fits a little further through the data with each one — and the Evaluator counts those crates away unscored, because teaching is not a test. "Test what it studied" deals those SAME days again, and this time the reader GUESSES: the Cups display says each number out loud and the Tally scores them under Training. "Test on new" deals the held-out Validation pile the same way, scored in its own column — the gap between those two numbers is the whole lesson. The Test pile has a release of its own and nothing is wired to it, on purpose: that pile is the sealed exam, and an exam you can re-take whenever you like is not an exam — drag a Button onto releaseTest when a teacher wants it opened. Each act ends with the Display counting the rows that act covered — a number, not a name. A Board stands beside the Evaluator, already watching the reader’s Polynomial degree — each test drops a point on it, so turn the dial and test again: the curve that shows overfitting starts to draw itself.

consensus.name: Two models, one observation
consensus.note: Two independently trained models read each Iris observation. Join waits for both readings; the counters show agreement and disagreement. Change a model or its confidence threshold and explain what changes.

carrules.name: Car rules
carrules.note:
Real cars — two Calculates derive horsepower per 1000 lb, and numeric Filters decide "sporty" or "economical" by a rule you can read

Twelve real cars from the 1970s and 80s: horsepower and weight, straight from the Files block down a wire — no belt at all, this machine is all signals. The first Calculate divides power by weight; the second multiplies by 1000 so the number is readable. That derived number is a NEW measurement nobody recorded — feature engineering, by hand. Two Filters read it: more than 40 lights Sporty and whistles, less than 32 lights Economical. The Window averages the last five cars. Change a threshold and predict which cars flip. Notice what this machine is NOT: there is no Model — a person wrote the rule. Ask what a Model could learn here that the rule cannot.

fuelforecast.name: Fuel Forecast
fuelforecast.note: The first of four benches in one garage: teach the machine how power and weight decide a car’s fuel use, then test it on cars it has never met.

designcar.name: Design the Car
designcar.note: The second of four benches in one garage: build a car that reaches the target mpg while its power stays under the limit.

pieces.name: Challenge 3 — under 120 hp and at least 3800 lbs

mysterycar.name: Mystery Car
mysterycar.note: The third of four benches in one garage: a real car hides behind one mpg figure — turn the dials until the machine predicts it.

garagedoor.name: Garage Door Guard
garagedoor.note: The last of four benches in one garage: the guard opens only for cars whose power and weight sit inside the range the machine learned from.

pieces.name: The guard opens only for power 40–250 hp and weight 1500–5500 lbs
